lines.text: A typesetting system takes a description of a document and decides where
every character goes. It breaks paragraphs into lines, stacks the lines into
pages and places headings, notes and figures where the reader expects them.
Each of these steps follows rules that can be written down precisely, and a
Lines of a paragraph are chosen together rather than one at a time. The
program looks at every way of breaking the paragraph and picks the one
whose lines are spaced most evenly, avoiding hyphens on consecutive lines
and very loose lines next to very tight ones.
Pages are built one line at a time. As each line arrives the program
measures how well the page would look if it ended there, and when adding
more would only make it worse it stops and starts a new page. Penal-
